exercises.heading: Section 6.5 Exercises
exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false.

problem.paragraph: If the coordinate functions of $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }:\mathbb{R}^{3}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ have continuous second partial derivatives, then $$\text{curl} ( \text{div} (\mathbf{ \text{F} }))$$ equals zero.

solution.paragraph: False

problem.paragraph: All vector fields of the form $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y,z} \right) = f(x)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + g(y)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + h(z)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ are conservative.

solution.paragraph: True

problem.paragraph: If F is a constant vector field then $$\text{div} \mathbf{ \text{F} } = 0.$$
If F is a constant vector field then $$\text{curl} \mathbf{ \text{F} } = 0.$$

solution.paragraph: True

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the curl of F.

solution.paragraph: $$curl F = i + x 2 j + y 2 k curl F = i + x 2 j + y 2 k$$
$$curl F = ( x z 2 - x y 2 ) i + ( x 2 y - y z 2 ) j + ( y 2 z - x 2 z ) k curl F = ( x z 2 - x y 2 ) i + ( x 2 y - y z 2 ) j + ( y 2 z - x 2 z ) k$$
$$curl F = i + j + k curl F = i + j + k$$
$$curl F = - y i - z j - x k curl F = - y i - z j - x k$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = ax\mathbf{ \text{i} } + by\mathbf{ \text{j} } + c\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ for constants a, b, c

solution.paragraph: $$curl F = 0 curl F = 0$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the divergence of F.

solution.paragraph: $$div F = 3 y z 2 + 2 y sin z + 2 x e 2 z div F = 3 y z 2 + 2 y sin z + 2 x e 2 z$$
$$div F = 2 ( x + y + z ) div F = 2 ( x + y + z )$$
$$div F = 1 x 2 + y 2 div F = 1 x 2 + y 2$$

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = ax\mathbf{ \text{i} } + by\mathbf{ \text{j} } + c\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ for constants a, b, c

solution.paragraph: $$div F = a + b div F = a + b$$
$$div F = x + y + z div F = x + y + z$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, determine whether each of the given scalar functions is harmonic.

solution.paragraph: Harmonic

problem.paragraph: If $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 2\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2x\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 3y\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{G} }(x,y,z) = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + z\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ find $$\text{curl} (\mathbf{ \text{F} } \times \mathbf{ \text{G} }).$$

If $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 2\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2x\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 3y\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{G} }(x,y,z) = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + z\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ find $$\text{div} (\mathbf{ \text{F} } \times \mathbf{ \text{G} }).$$

solution.paragraph: $$div ( F \times G ) = 2 z + 3 x div ( F \times G ) = 2 z + 3 x$$

problem.paragraph: Find $$\text{div} \mathbf{ \text{F} },$$ given that $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \text{∇} f,$$ where $$f(x,y,z) = xy^{3}z^{2}.$$

Find the divergence of F for vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = \left( {y^{2} + z^{2}} \right)\left( {x + y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {z^{2} + x^{2}} \right)\left( {y + z} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {x^{2} + y^{2}} \right)\left( {z + x} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$
Find the divergence of F for vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = f_{1}(y,z)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + f_{2}(x,z)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + f_{3}(x,y)\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use $$r = \left. ||\mathbf{ \text{r} } \right.||$$ and $$\textbf{r} = {< {x,y,z} >}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$curl r = 0 curl r = 0$$
$$curl r r 3 = 0 curl r r 3 = 0$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \frac{-y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} }}{x^{2} + y^{2}},$$ where F is defined on $$\left\{ (x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{2} \middle| (x,y) \neq (0,0) \right\}.$$ Find $$\text{curl} \mathbf{ \text{F} }.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use a computer algebra system to find the curl of the given vector fields.

solution.paragraph: $$curl F = 2 x x 2 + y 2 k curl F = 2 x x 2 + y 2 k$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the divergence of F at the given point.

solution.paragraph: $$div F = 0 div F = 0$$
$$div F = 0 div F = 0$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the curl of F at the given point.

solution.paragraph: $$curl F = j - 3 k curl F = j - 3 k$$
$$curl F = 2 j - k curl F = 2 j - k$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = \left( {3x^{2}y + az} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x^{3}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \left( {3x + 3z^{2}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$ For what value of a is F conservative?

Given vector field $$\textbf{F}(x,y) = \frac{1}{x^{2} + y^{2}}{< {-y,x} >}$$ on domain $$D = {\mathbb{R}}^{2} - \left\{ (0,0) \right\} = \left\{ (x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{2} \middle| (x,y) \neq (0,0) \right\},$$ is F conservative?

Given vector field $$\textbf{F}(x,y) = \frac{1}{x^{2} + y^{2}}{< {x,y} >}$$ on domain $$D = {\mathbb{R}}^{2} - \left\{ (0,0) \right\} = \left\{ (x,y) \in \mathbb{R}^{2} \middle| (x,y) \neq (0,0) \right\},$$ is F conservative?

solution.paragraph: F is conservative.

problem.paragraph: Find the work done by force field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = e^{-y}\mathbf{ \text{i} } - xe^{-y}\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ in moving an object from P(0, 1) to Q(2, 0). Is the force field conservative?
Compute the divergence of $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {\sinh x} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {\cosh y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } - xyz\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$

solution.paragraph: $$div F = cosh x + sinh y - x y div F = cosh x + sinh y - x y$$

problem.paragraph: Compute the curl of $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {\sinh x} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {\cosh y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } - xyz\mathbf{ \text{k} }.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, consider a rigid body that is rotating about the x-axis counterclockwise with constant angular velocity $$\omega = \left\langle {a,b,c} \right\rangle.$$ If P is a point in the body located at $$\mathbf{ \text{r} } = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + z\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ the velocity at P is given by vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \omega \times \mathbf{ \text{r} }.$$

problem.paragraph: Express F in terms of i, j, and k vectors.

solution.paragraph: $$( b z - c y ) i + ( c x - a z ) j + ( a y - b x ) k ( b z - c y ) i + ( c x - a z ) j + ( a y - b x ) k$$
$$curl F = 2 \omega curl F = 2 \omega$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, suppose that $$\nabla \cdot \mathbf{ \text{F} } = 0$$ and $$\nabla \cdot \mathbf{ \text{G} } = 0.$$

solution.paragraph: $$F\times GF\times G$$ does not have zero divergence.

problem.paragraph: [T] Consider rotational velocity field $$\mathbf{ \text{v} } = \left\langle {0,10z,-10y} \right\rangle.$$ If a paddlewheel is placed in plane $$x + y + z = 1$$ with its axis normal to this plane, using a computer algebra system, calculate how fast the paddlewheel spins in revolutions per unit of time.
